scenarios.title: Full spectrum
scenarios.blurb: All seven traffic classes over 30 minutes: every threat family the problem statement names, plus the benign hosts that make them hard to find.

scenarios.title: Clean traffic (negative control)
scenarios.blurb: No attacks at all. The correct output is almost nothing — a detector that fires on this is worthless. One alert survives, and it is the backup host we planted as a hard negative.

scenarios.title: Stealthy C2 only
scenarios.blurb: Command-and-control beaconing hidden in ordinary traffic, with jitter you can dial from 0 to 50 percent to watch the timing signal degrade.

scenarios.title: Exfiltration and tunnelling
scenarios.blurb: Data leaving by two different routes — bulk upload over TLS, and slow drip encoded into DNS queries.

scenarios.title: Volumetric and reconnaissance
scenarios.blurb: A spoofed-source flood and a fan-out port scan — the two loud classes, useful for showing source-entropy and breadth signals.

volumetric_ddos.title: Volumetric DDoS
volumetric_ddos.plain: A flood of traffic from many fake addresses trying to overwhelm a server so real users cannot reach it.
volumetric_ddos.analogy: Like thousands of hoax callers jamming a helpline so genuine callers get a busy tone.
volumetric_ddos.why: Can knock a public service — a bank portal, a power dashboard — offline for everyone.
volumetric_ddos.action: Rate-limit or block the source ranges upstream; alert the ISP.

c2_beaconing.title: C2 Beaconing
c2_beaconing.plain: A device on the network is quietly checking in with an attacker's server at regular intervals, waiting for orders.
c2_beaconing.analogy: Like a planted spy calling their handler at the same time every hour to receive instructions.
c2_beaconing.why: It is the heartbeat of an active intrusion — the attacker already has a foothold inside.
c2_beaconing.action: Isolate the device, capture the destination, hunt for how it got in.

dga_resolution.title: DGA Resolution
dga_resolution.plain: A device is looking up lots of random-looking website names — the way malware finds its command server when fixed addresses are blocked.
dga_resolution.analogy: Like a courier dialling hundreds of random numbers until the boss picks up.
dga_resolution.why: A strong sign of malware trying to reach its operator resiliently.
dga_resolution.action: Block the domains, quarantine the host, identify the malware family.

dns_tunnelling.title: DNS Tunnelling
dns_tunnelling.plain: Data is being smuggled out hidden inside ordinary-looking DNS lookups — a channel that often slips past firewalls.
dns_tunnelling.analogy: Like sneaking documents out of a building folded inside routine mail that nobody inspects.
dns_tunnelling.why: A covert exit route for stolen data or remote control.
dns_tunnelling.action: Block the domain, inspect the host, tighten DNS egress rules.

encrypted_malware.title: Malware in Encrypted Traffic
encrypted_malware.plain: An encrypted connection whose software fingerprint matches malware, not a normal browser — spotted without decrypting anything.
encrypted_malware.analogy: Like recognising a burglar by their gait on CCTV without ever opening the bag they carry.
encrypted_malware.why: Modern malware hides inside HTTPS; the fingerprint gives it away.
encrypted_malware.action: Investigate the host and destination; the payload was never opened.

recon_scanning.title: Reconnaissance / Port Scan
recon_scanning.plain: Someone is probing many ports on the network to map which doors are open — usually the first step before an attack.
recon_scanning.analogy: Like a burglar walking down a street trying every door and window to see which is unlocked.
recon_scanning.why: Early warning: an attacker is planning their way in.
recon_scanning.action: Note the source, review exposed services, watch for a follow-up.

data_exfiltration.title: Data Exfiltration
data_exfiltration.plain: A device is sending out far more data than it receives, to a place it never talked to before — the shape of data being stolen.
data_exfiltration.analogy: Like an employee who suddenly carries out boxes of files every night to an address the company has no dealings with.
data_exfiltration.why: This is the theft itself — intellectual property or citizen data leaving.
data_exfiltration.action: Cut the connection, preserve evidence, begin incident response.

benign.title: Benign
benign.plain: Normal, expected traffic. No action needed.
